question: A sector has a central angle of 135° and a radius of 8 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of (3pi)/(4) radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For sectors of the same circle, the area is directly proportional to the central angle.

Central angle of the first sector = 135°

Central angle of the second sector = (3π ÷ 4) radians = (3 ÷ 4) × 180° = 135°

Since both central angles are equal, the areas of both sectors are identical.

Ratio of their areas = 1 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 8 cm

Central angle of the first sector (θ₁) = 135°

Central angle of the second sector (θ₂) = 3π ÷ 4 radians

**Formula Used:**

Area of a sector (in degrees) = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Area of a sector (in radians) = (1 ÷ 2) × θ × r²

 
 

 
 r = 8 cm

 r = 8 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the first sector (A₁) = (135° ÷ 360°) × π × (8)²

⇒ A₁ = (3 ÷ 8) × 64π = 24π cm²

⇒ Area of the second sector (A₂) = (1 ÷ 2) × (3π ÷ 4) × (8)²

⇒ A₂ = (3π ÷ 8) × 64 = 24π cm²

⇒ Ratio of their areas = A₁ : A₂

⇒ Ratio = 24π : 24π = 1 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

When the central angle θ is in degrees: Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr². When θ is in radians: Area = (1 ÷ 2) × θr².

Arc Length of a Sector

When θ is in degrees: Arc length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr. When θ is in radians: Arc length = r × θ.

Angle Conversions

Degrees to Radians: Multiply the degree value by (π ÷ 180°). Radians to Degrees: Multiply the radian value by (180° ÷ π).
